source: issue #77; verify-78. Tolerance: v_at_enable exact, because V_CURRENT is a line counter and the read sees a neighbor line only when a line change falls inside the read, which would also put first_ticks under one poll period. first_ticks abs:14, one console poll period: the first-change loops are each lw V_CURRENT, beq, nop (asm.py k_vi_enable), so a reading lands on the poll grid and a correct model can differ from the console by one period. The sync loop that waits for vertical blank is lw, sltiu, bnez, nop, one instruction longer (asm.py kve_vblank); its period is not in the bound, and whether its phase widens first_ticks depends on #77, which this question decides. The period is at most 28 pclk: an RCP register read is at most 25 pclk: n64-systembench RCP I/O R, 24 pclk on VI_CONTROL, plus main.c's 1-cycle sampling error (main.c:571, 18, 649-654 @50f5066); beq reads the loaded register, and a reader of the loaded register in the next slot adds the 1 pclk load interlock, which stays active through a data-cache miss and adds one clock after it (VR4300 User's Manual U10504EJ7V0UM00 4.6.5, Fig. 4-17); the kit assumes the same for an uncached load, which also stalls in DC on the System interface (12.1; inferred, and the bound only grows by it); then beq and nop. COUNT runs at half PClock (VR4300 User's Manual 6.3.3), so 2 pclk = 1 tick: 28 pclk = 14 ticks. Not derived from the fork's spread over boot delays

question: How many COUNT ticks is one NTSC VI field (X1 vs X2 ratio, crystal error)? The kit's VI (V_SYNC 0x20D progressive, H_SYNC 0xC15) runs 263 lines of 3094 VCLK, 783,520.9 ticks at VCLK 48.681812 MHz and COUNT 46.875 MHz; the fork reads 783,516-783,530
decides: COUNT over 60 fields, and the shortest and longest field
source: hardware-corpora.md #24; clocks.md; verify-85 2a.7 (its 782,031 assumed 262.5 lines, the interlaced count). Tolerance rel:0.01203 (120.3 ppm): X1 and X2 are separate KDS AT-49 crystals (n64brew Clock_Timing), each within 30 ppm at 25 C plus 30 ppm over -10..+60 C, the datasheet's tightest grades (KDS AT-38/AT-49 2011-2012 catalog p32; the fitted grade is not published, so a looser grade is possible). The VCLK/COUNT ratio can then be off by (1+60e-6)/(1-60e-6)-1 = 120.0 ppm, plus one 29 pclk poll period (lw 24+1 pclk per main.c:571 @50f5066, the 1 pclk load interlock of sltu on the loaded register per VR4300 User's Manual 4.6.5, then sltu, beqz, move) over 60 fields = 0.3 ppm. Aging is not published, so a console whose crystals drifted past spec fails and the detail shows its ratio. The AT-49 is identified only from motherboard photos (n64brew Clock_Timing), and the catalog's wider grades give 200 ppm (+-50 and +-50) or 400 ppm (+-100 and +-100). So a console fail between 120 ppm and about 323 ppm is read from the ratio in the detail line, as an unknown crystal grade, not as a model defect. 120 ppm still separates the alternatives the row is about: one VCLK per line is 323 ppm, interlaced vs progressive line count 1900 ppm

question: When the earliest pending request goes to the device a write just used (inside NEC tPostMemWriteDelay) and a later one goes to another device, which does the RI grant first (ri.post-write-gap's arbitration readings A, B and C)?
decides: the summed ticks of 32 uncached CPU loads (min over 4 reps) while an RDP fill writes bank 7 and a 16 KiB SP DMA reads bank 6, both device 3, with the loads in bank 5 (device 2) and in bank 6 (device 3). After each fill write the SP DMA's next burst is the earliest request and is in the write's gap. Readings (PR #137, verify-137): B, the fork, waits for the gap and grants the earliest; A commits to the first-edge winner and then waits; C grants a request to another device first. With the loads in device 2, A reads as B and C lower, because each load skips the gapped SP burst (boot-1: B and A 1486..1572, C 1040..1090, U-KIT-LAST-POINTS). With the loads in device 3 every pending request is gapped and the three read the same (1292..1317), the control. A differs from B only when a VI fetch or a refresh, which outrank the CPU and the DMAs, arrives in the 1 rclk gap; no point here makes that happen, so this question separates C from A and B, not A from B
source: verify-137; NEC M10801EJ4V0DSU1 p44; U-KIT-LAST-POINTS (prehw-plan.md section 4). Tolerance 32 ticks: each of the 32 loads is timed between two MFC0 COUNT reads, and COUNT ticks once per 2 pclk (VR4300 User's Manual 6.3.3), so a load's reading is off its time by under 1 tick and the sum by under 32. The fork's spread over boot delays and layout pads covers the phase; the tolerance is only the reading's quantization

question: How long after V_CURRENT reaches V_INTR does MI_INTR show the VI interrupt (#24)?
decides: a poll loop reading MI_INTR then V_CURRENT, its phase walked over 16 reps: V_CURRENT at the first poll that saw the interrupt (field bit cleared, #132) and the mean lag in ticks (fork 256 and about 11-15; a half-line or end-of-line interrupt shows about 1490 or 2979). Under about 6 ticks does not resolve: the poll is 31 ticks
source: issue #16 (from #24). Tolerance: v_at_intr exact, because V_CURRENT is a line counter and the loop reads it within a few poll periods of the line start, far less than the 2979-tick line, so a correct model reads the same line; a half-line or end-of-line interrupt reads another line, which is what the row decides. vintr-mean-lag abs:33, one poll period: each rep's lag is a whole number of loop iterations, and for one true lag a rep reads one of two adjacent grid values, so the console's trimmed mean and a correct model's differ by less than the longest iteration. That is the iteration that first sees V_CURRENT == V_INTR: two RCP reads (MI_INTR, V_CURRENT), an RCP register read is at most 25 pclk: n64-systembench RCP I/O R, 24 pclk on VI_CONTROL, plus main.c's 1-cycle sampling error (main.c:571, 18, 649-654 @50f5066), and 16 single-cycle instructions (no load-use slot: andi reads the first load two slots later), 66 pclk. COUNT runs at half PClock (VR4300 User's Manual 6.3.3), so 2 pclk = 1 tick: 33 ticks. MI_INTR's read cost is inferred from VI_CONTROL's (same RCP register bus; kit question cpu-reads measures it). The phase walk (VINTR_STEP) rides on bus_vwait_eq's own poll, so no sub-period bound is claimed. The old abs:6 had no basis and was under one period

question: What does one SP DMA of 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 B cost per direction, timed by the RSP on its own clock (the CPU's poll and register-write rate cannot resolve them, verify-85 2a.5)?
decides: an RSP program in IMEM writes SP_MEM_ADDR and SP_DRAM_ADDR, reads DPC_CLOCK (COP0 $12, RCP clocks), writes SP_RD_LEN (rd, RDRAM to DMEM) or SP_WR_LEN (wr) and polls SP_DMA_BUSY (COP0 $6) with mfc0, bne, nop, then reads DPC_CLOCK again; 8 blocks per run put 0..7 extra NOPs before the first poll, and min is the least block over 4 runs, in RCP clocks, walk_max the greatest block of the last run. poll is the same program with an SP_DRAM_ADDR rewrite for the trigger: the RSP's fixed cost from the clock read to the poll's exit with no DMA. A wr or rd min equal to poll's means the DMA ended before the first poll could see it. VI blanked. The fork reads poll 9, rd 10 11 14 17 25, wr 9 10 12 16 24 (u-spdma)
source: green-plan pending.md section 2 (sp-dma-direction), U-SPDMA; u-spdma. Tolerance abs:6 RCP clocks, one period of the RSP poll loop: mfc0 runs in 1 cycle with a 3-cycle latency, so the bne that reads it next stalls 2 cycles; a branch runs in 3 cycles counting its delay slot, one being the bubble that finalizes it (n64brew Reality_Signal_Processor/CPU_Pipeline, write latency and branches): mfc0 1 + stall 2 + bne 1 + nop 1 + bubble 1 = 6. A reading lands on that poll grid, so without the walk a correct model and the console differ by under one period; the 1-clock NOP walk over 8 blocks covers a 6-clock period, so the walk's min only tightens it. DPC_CLOCK counts RCP clocks and an RSP MFC0 of it reads the RSP's cycle count (nemu64-test rsp_timing ClockCPUvsRSP: 100000 COUNT ticks read 133333 +-20; CyclesSLL: an SLL between two reads costs 1). The fork stalls a taken branch one cycle after its delay slot too (RSP::instructionEpilogue pipeline.stall(); verify-124 measured 6 rclk per taken loop iteration), so its period is also 6. Not derived from the fork's spread over boot delays. The band is wider than the walk resolves: a fork build with ri.read-hit and ri.write-hit each 1 rclk longer reads every rd and wr min 1-2 higher and still passes (u-spdma), so a pass does not verify ri.read-hit or ri.write-hit; read each point's console and model min in the pass detail before calling it agreement. Adding this kernel to kit-dma moved every kit-dma point by layout (#100), so pi-dma-rowend/cart-to-ram-128-off7c0 min went from 1198 to 1203 at all 8 boot delays and pi-row-end (range:abs:4) compares the console against 1203, not 1198 (verify-124)

question: Do SC and SCD on this console give the VR4300 User's Manual's stated results (cpu-llsc's 12 self-checked cases), and does an SC or SCD that fails (LLbit clear) to an address WatchLo matches raise Watch?

question: Is a span RAM half reusable once each 16 B segment's write-back lands, or only once the whole 64 B half's has (span-ram.md row 6, open question 4)?
decides: DPC_CLOCK of 256-line 1-cycle write-only rectangles (no IM_RD, no Z) at every width 1-80 px, at 32 and 16 bpp, each line its own 2 KiB RDRAM row (color image 512 px at 32 bpp, 1024 px at 16 bpp). A width is a step when its clock exceeds the previous width's by more than 256 rclk (one pixel per line at rdp.span-1cycle's 1 px/rclk) plus 143.4 rclk; release is the most common spacing of the steps: segment (4 px at 32 bpp, 8 px at 16 bpp), half (16 px, 32 px), no-step, period-<px> for any other spacing or single-<width> for one step. The 32 bpp value decides the item; the 16 bpp value also hangs on a 16 bpp half's size (color-half-16bpp), so period-16 there is a 16 px half. steady_half, the 32 bpp cost per 64 B half, (clock at 320 px - clock at 160 px) / (256 lines x 10 halves), is compared: it decides rdp.mem-overhead-write, which holds the memory port for each 64 B write-back's wire time plus 19.5 rclk, so the fork reads 29.0 against the 16 clocks a 32 bpp half shades in (u-span-kit report, measured); the steps' widths are report values
source: U-SPAN-KIT (docs/research/span-ram-attempt.md); steady_half U-WRITE-HOLD-Q (docs/design/prehw-plan.md section 4 Q2). Tolerance: exact on the release category; abs 0.76 rclk on steady_half, derived as mem-overhead-pipelined's threshold and band, refresh share and instrument both: (1) count jitter: the two clock reads err by at most one poll period and two refreshes, (20.4 + 2 x 61.5) / 2560 halves = 0.056. (2) refresh share: the fork reads 28.9988 with no refresh at all, since the rectangles run vi=off and the fork refreshes only while the VI is active (ri.refresh-trigger; verify-159 measured 28.9988 unchanged with ri.refresh-dirty at 52 and 62). A console may refresh here: ri.refresh-trigger's open SOURCE CONFLICT cites rdram-bus-arbitration.md B11, refresh before VI init at H_TOTAL 0x7FF, about 42 us = 2625 rclk per line. At that rate and the largest cited cost, ri.refresh-dirty 54 plus ri.retry-dirty 7.5 = 61.5 rclk (B12 clean 52 is smaller), refresh takes 61.5 / 2625 = 2.34% of the time, so a console with the fork's write hold reads 28.9988 / (1 - 0.0234) = 29.6945, 0.6957 above the fork (54 rclk alone: 0.6091); with no refresh at blank (nemu64's reading, the fork's choice) it reads 28.9988. Every cited assumption lies in 0..0.6957 of refresh share, so 0.6957 + 0.056 = 0.7517, rounded up to 0.76: a correct write hold reads 28.9428..29.7505 and passes under either side of the conflict. The band is symmetric because the rule is (range:abs); its low side is wider than any cited cause needs. derived.py keeps 4 places, so its rounding adds at most 0.0001. An earlier band, abs 0.06, held the jitter only (verify-159: a console refreshing at B11's rate would fail it with the correct write hold); this one was fixed from the terms above before any mutation was compared with it (U-WRITE-HOLD-Q fix round). The plan-fixed mutations of rdp.mem-overhead-write to 15 and 24 rclk read 24.9957 and 34.0008 against the fork's 28.9988 at every boot delay and layout pad (U-WRITE-HOLD-Q report, measured). Under abs 0.76 they lie 5.27 and 6.58 tolerances out, past U-SEPARATES' bound of 4, so the separating mutation is a step up that moves steady_half past 2 tolerances (the metric jumps between 20.75 and 21, verify-159b, measured): 20.5 reads 29.998 (1.31), 21.5 reads 31.0043 (2.64), 22.5 reads 32.0031 (3.95); 21 also reads 31.0043 (each value at all 8 layout pads x 8 boot delays, U-WRITE-HOLD-Q fix round, measured; that the half's cost moves in whole rclk steps is inferred from 21 and 21.5 reading the same). The 16 bpp cost per half is not compared: a 16 bpp half shades in 32 clocks, above the fork's write cost, and its size is color-half-16bpp's open question. The step threshold is the instrument's, not the fork's: two adjacent widths' DPC_CLOCK reads each land up to one poll period late, at most 20.4 rclk (rdp-rect-base: lw MI_INTR, andi, beqz, nop), and a rectangle that grows by less than one refresh interval sees at most one refresh fewer or two more, each at most 61.5 rclk (ri.refresh-dirty 54 rclk plus the row retry ri.retry-dirty 30 tc = 7.5 rclk), so a width without a stall exceeds 256 rclk by at most 20.4 + 2 x 61.5 = 143.4 rclk; a stall of one RCP clock on each of 256 identical lines adds 256 rclk and clears it even with the error the other way (256 - 20.4 - 61.5 = 174.1). Why the older points cannot decide it: span-width (kit-span) has IM_RD on, so its steps mix reads and write-backs; kit-zmem zmem-slots' plain points are write-only but 16 bpp only, where a 64 B half is 32 px (32 shading clocks against about 28.5 rclk to write it back with the fitted rdp.mem-overhead-write, so even a per-half release need not stall; inferred) and the half's size is itself open; both sample widths 8 px or more apart, which alias a 4 or 8 px period, and run 8 lines, so a 1 rclk per line stall is 8 rclk, under one poll period; and both draw into a 320 px image, whose lines cross 2 KiB rows at width-dependent places

question: Does the RDP's per-transaction memory overhead (rdp.mem-overhead-read 21, rdp.mem-overhead-write 19.5 rclk, both fit) hold the memory port until it ends (occupancy, as the fork models it), or only delay that transaction's data while the next transaction starts after the RI wire time (pipelined latency)?
decides: DPC_CLOCK of span-write-release's 256-line 32 bpp rectangles with IM_RD on, 1-320 px: the steady cost per 64 B half, (clock at 320 px - clock at 160 px) / (256 lines x 10 halves), against 21.6 rclk, what one 64 B read and one 64 B write-back need on the RDRAM wire. port is wire-bound at or under it: the overhead does not hold the port in a steady line, which refutes occupancy (pipelined latency, or no overhead). It is above-wire over it: what occupancy predicts (about 60 rclk with the fit values); a pipelined RDP with too few span halves to cover its read and write latency also gives it (inferred), so above-wire alone does not prove occupancy and the steady_half value, a report value, is read against the read plus write hold. one_half_read, the cost a 16 px line's single read adds over the write-only rectangle, per line, is a report value
source: U-SPAN-KIT (docs/research/span-ram-attempt.md). Tolerance: exact on a category. The threshold is the NEC datasheet's wire time, not a fit: a 64 B read is ri.read-hit 10 + 8 x ri.octbyte 4 + ri.post-read-gap 2 = 44 tc and a 64 B write ri.write-hit 4 + 32 + ri.post-write-gap 4 = 40 tc, 84 tc = 21 rclk at 4 tc per rclk (clocks.md: RDRAM 250 MHz, RCP 62.5 MHz); every line is one row, so after its first access every transfer is a row hit. A 32 bpp half shades in 16 clocks, under 21. Refresh takes at most 61.5 rclk (ri.refresh-dirty plus ri.retry-dirty) per VI line, at least 42 us = 2625 rclk (rdram-bus-arbitration.md B11), 2.3% of the channel: 21 / (1 - 0.0234) = 21.5; the two clock reads err by at most one poll period and two refreshes, (20.4 + 2 x 61.5) / 2560 halves = 0.06: 21.6

question: When a VI line is shorter than the 52 rclk refresh holdoff, does the RI keep one refresh request and drop an HSYNC that comes while a refresh waits or runs, or does it queue every HSYNC's request (ri.refresh-latch)?
decides: H_SYNC 9, 19 and 35 (lines of 10, 20 and 36 VCLK: 0.25, 0.5 and 0.9 of the holdoff), no line in V_VIDEO, then an 8 B SP DMA polled 4096 times from the I-cache: starved 1 when it never finished. One latch (the fork) holds the channel at most 52 rclk of every 2 to 6 lines and the DMA finishes (starved 0); a queue gains a request each line and drains one per 52 rclk, so the refresh, which outranks every client, never lets the DMA in (starved 1, and the point restores H_SYNC instead of hanging the ROM). The timed loads that follow log lines per holdoff as report values (the fork 5.0, 3.0 and 2.0, bus-derived/hsync); they are not compared, since whether a burst in flight at an HSYNC pushes the holdoff past the next line depends on fitted RI overheads
source: rdram-bus-arbitration.md B11 (one SetRR per HSYNC); followups verify-57; docs/design/prehw-plan.md section 4 U-VI-SHORT-LINE. Tolerance: exact, because starved is a 0/1 verdict. With one latch a refresh is posted only at an HSYNC after the last one ended, so the DMA, waiting when it ends, is decided first; 4096 polls of at least 24 pclk (n64-systembench RCP I/O R) are 98,304 pclk (1.05 ms at 93.75 MHz), over 1,200 holdoffs of 54 rclk

question: When a VI line ends before its fetch does, does the line keep fetching while the next lines fetch nothing, or does each HSYNC drop the bursts not yet posted (vi.fetch-overrun)?
decides: H_SYNC 399 (lines of 400 VCLK, shorter than H_START's 432 VCLK, so each line ends before its first burst is due) with vi_init's V_VIDEO, against the same window with no line in V_VIDEO, both from the next field (V_VIDEO latches per field, vi.frame-latch): the VI time is the loads the second window gains at its mean load period, and fetched is 1 when that exceeds one 54 rclk holdoff plus each window's longest load. A line that keeps fetching (the fork) fetches its 15 bursts over 8 lines (14.6 COUNT ticks of VI time per line on the fork, a report value); a VI that drops them at each HSYNC never posts one (fetched 0)
source: vi-fetch.md; docs/design/prehw-plan.md section 4 U-VI-SHORT-LINE. Tolerance: exact on a 0/1 verdict whose threshold is derived, not fitted: with no VI burst both windows last the same ticks and hold one refresh per 400 VCLK line (513 rclk, longer than a holdoff), so their refresh counts differ by at most one, at most 54 rclk = 40.5 COUNT ticks (n64brew RDRAM_Interface; RCP 62.5 MHz, n64brew Clock_Timing; COUNT at half the 93.75 MHz PClock, VR4300 User's Manual 6.3.3), and each window ends on the one load that crosses it, at most that window's lat_max
